audience: first-time homeowners in the week after closing, keys in hand, no idea what the house needs
homeowners in freezing northern US states pinning fall and winterizing lists in September and October
people who keep forgetting home maintenance and want to be told what needs them this week
home-binder and household-binder makers who print checklists and fill them in by hand
renters moving into an apartment who want the deposit back and the notice date remembered
the person in the house who gets asked 'where is the water shutoff?' and 'what size is the filter?'

visualWorld.setting: The house itself, drawn the way the Home Survey book draws it: an architect's section through an ordinary two-storey American house with a basement, laid on warm drawing paper with registration ticks in the corners and a faint squared grid (both taken from the Home Survey printable, src/products/home-management-companion/printables/workbook.tsx: Ticks and GridField). Every pin is a sheet from that drawing set: a whole-house section, a close-up plate of one object, the fridge door in the kitchen, the open binder, the year as a wheel. Renter pins switch the section for an apartment floor plan.

props.draw: Front section of a two-storey gable house: outer wall as a 14px warm-paper band, pitched roof as two straight slopes with a 3px shingle hatch, gutter as a small U channel at each eave, downspout as a thin vertical rectangle ending in an elbow. Inside: four rooms (kitchen, laundry/utility, bedroom with hallway, living room) as flat tinted rectangles, an attic triangle with insulation as a soft zigzag fill, a basement band below a 6px ground line with soil as a stipple of 4px dots. Fixtures are simple silhouettes placed where they really live; callouts are 2px ink leader lines ending in a 10px open circle on the object and a label block in the margin.

Same drawing language as house-cutaway but a single-floor flat: one storey box, no roof slope, no gutters, one exterior wall with a window. Optional ghost: the roof and gutters of a house drawn as a 2px dashed outline only, to show what renter setup stops asking about.

Tall rounded rectangle cabinet with a front louvre panel (5 short horizontal slots), a flue pipe rising from the top as a narrow rectangle with one elbow, a slot on the side where the filter slides in, shown with the filter edge sticking out 12px.

Flat rectangle in 3/4 view: cardboard frame as a 22px border in kraft tan, pleated media inside as a zigzag polyline in off-white, an airflow arrow printed on the frame, and the size '16x25x1' printed on the frame in condensed caps. Optional grey-tone duplicate for a used filter.

Upright cylinder (rectangle with elliptical top cap), cold and hot pipes as two vertical lines from the top, the pressure relief valve as a small lever on the side with a discharge pipe running down, a drain valve near the base as a tiny spout, and a rating label as a small white rectangle near the top.

Wall-hung white box with rounded corners, a small display rectangle and two dials, pipes leaving the bottom; one radiator elsewhere drawn as 6 vertical rounded fins with a bleed key at the top corner.

A horizontal pipe crossing the frame. Ball-valve version: a flat lever handle, drawn along the pipe for open and across the pipe for closed. Gate-valve version: a round wheel handle with 5 spokes on a short stem. A strip of bright tape wrapped round the pipe beside it, and an optional paper tag on a string.

Hose bib on a siding wall: a short spout with a round or cross handle, a garden hose as a thick curved line coiled into 3 loops on the ground, an optional foam cover as a rounded dome over the bib. Winter variant: icicle triangles under the spout.

A copper pipe in section inside a wall cavity (two vertical stud rectangles either side, pink insulation zigzag). Before: pipe with a blue water channel. After: a pale ice plug, a jagged split line along the pipe wall, and three water drops falling. No flames, no tools.
Eave close-up: gutter as a U-channel profile, leaves as small almond shapes piled inside, downspout dropping to an elbow and a splash block pointing away from the foundation line.
Ceiling disc: circle with an inner ring of 8 vent slots, a small test button circle, a tiny indicator dot in the accent colour.
Dryer as a square cabinet with a round door; flexible duct behind it as a ribbed tube (series of parallel arcs) running to an outside flap hood on the wall.

A refrigerator front filling most of the pin: rounded rectangle, one long vertical handle bar, a freezer split line in the top third, flat off-white enamel colour with a very soft highlight stripe. It is a noticeboard: paper, cards and magnets sit on it.

A torn notepad sheet (straight top, slightly ragged bottom via a 6-point polyline) held by two magnets, with ruled lines and square checkboxes; text set in the pin's sans, not fake handwriting. Variants: a single sticky square, a two-column 'keep / leave out' sheet.
Small flat shapes with a 4px drop shadow: a circle, a little house pentagon, and a business-card rectangle with blank lines (no invented company names or numbers).

A paper card, slightly rotated (-3deg), with a header line and six label/value rows in the order the real printable uses: Brand, Model, Location, What to buy, Installed, Warranty expires (src/products/home-management-companion/printables/generateItemCard.tsx FIELD_LABEL). A hole punch circle top-left.
Silver-grey rectangle with 4 rivet dots in the corners, rows of condensed caps: MODEL, SERIAL, VOLTS / WATTS, and a small square for the QR/barcode block.

Open three-ring binder seen from above: two page rectangles, three rings as circles down the gutter, coloured tab dividers sticking out of the right edge as rounded rectangles with short labels. The right page shows one Home Survey plate: plate number in small caps, a serif title, ruled fields, and the registration ticks in its corners.

A donut ring split into 12 wedges, January at 12 o'clock. Wedge fill strength = number of seasonal jobs that month (Plate 15 counts). Empty months stay paper-coloured with a tiny 'Clear' label. A highlighted wedge can be pulled out 24px from the ring. Centre disc holds one seasonal glyph (leaf for autumn, snowflake for winter, bud for spring) and at most one short line.
Open-top carry box: trapezoid body, central handle bar, a few tool silhouettes sticking up (screwdriver, adjustable wrench, a roll of tape, a torch). Used as a stand for the phone-screen.

Plain rounded-rectangle phone frame (no brand), 40px corner radius, holding one real screenshot from creative/public/screens/home-management-companion-*.png cropped above the dev overlay (the black 'N' badge and the 'Start' bar near y=790-840 on the 390px-wide captures must be cropped out).
Box unit sitting in a window frame: front grille as horizontal slats, two small dials; winter variant is the same box on a shelf with a dust cover outline.
Furnace-mounted humidifier as a small box on the duct, with the pad pulled out beside it: a rectangle with a honeycomb/diamond texture.
Sprinkler head as a short cylinder in a grass strip, with dashed lines for the buried line and an arrow showing air blown through it.

Where a pipe enters the wall: a pencil-width gap drawn as a dark sliver, with a small round mouse silhouette (two circle ears, long tail line) outside it; after-state shows the gap filled with a caulk bead.

Season markers: almond leaves in two warm tones for autumn, a six-armed snowflake and a thermometer reading 32°F for the hard freeze (the National Weather Service threshold cited in the winterize guide).

Top-down plan of a one-bedroom flat: 6px walls, door swings as quarter arcs, kitchen counter run with a sink circle, bath with tub rectangle. Camera viewfinder corner brackets drawn in each room, and a numbered dotted walking path through the rooms.
Flat photo frames (no photography): a white border with a drawn close-up inside, e.g. a wall with a scuff, the inside of an oven, a window latch, a carpet edge. A small date stamp in the corner.
A paper card captioned 'The lease' with ruled fields Started / Renews on / Notice by, beside a second card 'The deposit' with Amount / Held by / Returned in (Home Survey Plate 19).
The 'before' scatter: an envelope, a half-open drawer with a receipt sticking out, a thought cloud with a blank calendar square in it.
Two shelf planks with three or four furnace filters standing on edge, each with a different blank size label, and one with '16x25x1' highlighted.
A tall paint swatch strip with three colour blocks and two ruled lines labelled Room and Colour and code (Home Survey Plate 16).
Flat-lay of the Home Survey's 'What to bring': a torch, a phone, a cloth, the book, a pen, and a small clock face for half an hour.

visualWorld.palette: Built on Home Base's own accent and the Home Survey's palette, not a new scheme. Paper #f4f2ec (manifest background) and #fbfaf6 (survey paper); ink #1a2420; sage #4f7a5c as the one accent (product accent), sage deep #3d6149 for headline emphasis, sage soft #e6ede2 for room fills and calm panels; ochre #8a5a11 with ochre soft #f6edda only for 'needs a look' and SAFETY tags (the product's own warm warning, as in the workspace screen); kraft tan for filters, cards and cardboard. One cool tone, a muted slate blue, is allowed only for water and ice. Autumn pins may add the peach of the Seasons screen's 'This season' card, sampled from home-management-companion-seasons.png. No red, no alarm colours, no countdown numbers.
visualWorld.mood: Calm competence: a well-kept technical drawing of your own house, the feeling of finally knowing where things are. Light, roomy and precise, with thin 2-3px lines rather than the thick cartoon outlines of the shared finds template. Never alarmist, never 'overdue' (the product forbids the word), never a disaster photo. Even the frozen pipe is drawn as a diagram, not a catastrophe.

archetypes.name: Labelled house cutaway
archetypes.clicks: Home-maintenance pins are saved as reference. A house with labelled spots answers 'what is in my house and where' at a glance, the same question the shutoff and home-binder guidance says people should mark on a plan (abuyerschoice.com on marking shutoffs). Pinterest's own advice is that the topic must be obvious from the image on a phone, and a labelled house is legible even at thumbnail size. Infographic-style how-to content is among the formats Tailwind and Pinterest's business community report being saved.
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500. Headline block y 60-320, left-aligned at x 60, serif, max 3 lines, ink with one phrase in sage deep. House section centred, x 90-910, y 360-1180. Up to 6 callouts: 2px leader lines from a 10px ring on the object to label blocks in the left (x 40-250) and right (x 750-960) margins; each label is the item label in bold sans 30px over its task or fact in 24px. Optional phone-screen at x 60-330, y 1000-1440, overlapping the basement. Product line bottom-left at y 1360-1440 ('Home Base' wordmark + sub, max 2 lines), right edge no further than x 780 so the lower-right 200x200 stays clear for Pinterest's icons.
archetypes.visual: The house-cutaway (or apartment-section for renters) with the relevant fixtures drawn in their real places and only the called-out ones in full colour; everything else stays in pale sage-soft line so the eye goes to the labels.
archetypes.text: Headline = the pin's existing title. Callout labels = item labels and care task names from HOME_ITEM_TYPES in src/products/home-management-companion/homeKnowledge.ts, or real rows from the screenshots, or lines from the linked guide. Sub = a sentence from the pin's own description.
archetypes.bestFor: what is in your house, what matters most, ranked by consequence, new-homeowner setup, where the shutoff/plates are, history pinned to things, winterizing tour, renter setup

archetypes.name: The year as a wheel
archetypes.clicks: Month-by-month and seasonal calendars are the dominant packaging for home-maintenance printables in search results (monthly/seasonal/yearly checklists from Prudent Reviews, Scattered Squirrel, Free Organizing Printables, onotto's 'seasonal tasks'), and seasonal pins are searched well ahead of the season (Simple Pin Media: pin about 45 days ahead; Tailwind: 60-90 days). A wheel is that calendar as one graphic shape, which reads at thumbnail size and makes empty months visible.
archetypes.layout: Headline y 60-300, centred, serif, max 3 lines. Wheel centred at (500, 800), outer radius 380, ring width 140; month initials on the ring. Highlighted wedge(s) pulled out 24px with a leader to a job card. Job card y 1210-1400, x 60-780: 2-5 real jobs with their item label, 26px sans. Product line y 1410-1460 bottom-left.
archetypes.visual: year-wheel with fill strength from Plate 15 counts (Jan 0, Feb 1, Mar 4, Apr 9, May 8, Jun 1, Jul 0, Aug 0, Sep 10, Oct 11, Nov 2, Dec 0), plus leaf-and-frost markers. Empty wedges labelled 'Clear'.
archetypes.text: Month names, counts ('Clear', '1 job', '10 jobs' as Plate 15 prints them) and job names from HOME_ITEM_TYPES care templates that carry months; the line 'Nothing seasonal. A good month.' from workbook.tsx SeasonalPage.
archetypes.bestFor: calendar pins, empty months, date jobs vs interval jobs, gutters in December, furnace service timing

archetypes.name: The list on the fridge
archetypes.clicks: Printable checklist pins are the staple of this niche ('free printable home maintenance checklist' is how almost every result is framed), and checklists are one of the formats Tailwind and Pinterest's business community name as getting saves. Putting the list on a fridge door makes it a home object rather than a document, and it is the place a household actually keeps one.
archetypes.layout: Headline top full-width y 60-300. Fridge-door x 300-960, y 320-1500 (bleeds off the bottom edge). Fridge-note pinned at x 360-880, y 420-1250 with 4-7 rows: checkbox, task in 30px sans, optional small grey reason/month tag in 22px. One or two magnets and at most one extra card. Left strip x 40-280 holds the product line and sub, vertically centred near y 1250-1440, so nothing important sits in the lower-right corner.
archetypes.visual: fridge-door with fridge-note and magnets; optionally an item-card or business-card magnet. Ticks on 0-2 rows at most, so the list looks usable, not finished.
archetypes.text: List rows = real tasks: from the linked guide's own list (src/content/guides.ts), from HOME_ITEM_TYPES care templates, or rows visible on the real workspace screenshot. Reason lines use the product's real voice ('Last done 6 months ago, usually every 6 months').
archetypes.bestFor: fall and winterize lists, first-day lists, 'what's due this week', write-the-problem-down, keep/leave-out lists

archetypes.name: Close-up plate of one object
archetypes.clicks: The questions people search here are concrete and object-shaped: what size filter, where is the model number, which way does the valve turn. A single object drawn large with the fact printed on it ('16x25x1', MODEL / SERIAL, lever across the pipe) is the answer itself, which is what makes a reference pin worth saving. Pinterest advises a big, clear subject over a busy composition for mobile feeds.
archetypes.layout: Headline y 60-300. Object drawn at scale, centred, y 340-1120, taking ~65% of the width, with up to 3 short callouts. An item-card or note card overlaps the object's lower-left at -3deg, x 60-520, y 1050-1400. Product line bottom-left y 1410-1460.
archetypes.visual: furnace-filter, water-heater, model-plate, or main-shutoff-valve, drawn like a Home Survey plate with registration ticks and a faint grid behind it.
archetypes.text: The fact printed on the object, field labels from the Item Card or the Home Survey, and example values taken from the linked guide's own example table (e.g. 16x25x1 from how-often-change-furnace-filter).
archetypes.bestFor: filter size, model number, item card, repair diagnosis on the water heater, shutoff valve types

archetypes.name: The open home binder
archetypes.clicks: Home binders are an established Pinterest genre (household/home management binders, emergency info pages at the front, tabbed sections: The Homes I Have Made's Family HUB, Scattered Squirrel's emergency contacts printables, Etsy binder kits). The tabs themselves communicate 'organised' and the open page shows exactly what you'd fill in, which is why binder pins get saved for later.
archetypes.layout: Headline y 60-300. Binder open flat, centred, y 340-1330, rotated 0deg; tabs on the right page edge, x 880-960, one per section. Right page shows one plate with its real plate number, title and 4-8 ruled fields; left page shows the table of contents or the tab names. Product line bottom-left y 1360-1450.
archetypes.visual: survey-binder with real Home Survey plate content; optional walk-kit items at the margin.
archetypes.text: Plate numbers, titles and field labels exactly as workbook.tsx prints them (Plate 01 'If something goes wrong tonight.', Plate 15 'What belongs to which month.', Plate 18 'The home's memory.', Plate 19 'The dates that cost money to miss.'), or the five binder sections from the how-to-make-a-home-binder guide.
archetypes.bestFor: home binder pins, the Home Survey printable, emergency page, maintenance log page, twelve areas

archetypes.name: Then and now panels
archetypes.clicks: Step-by-step and before/after are the core how-to shapes on Pinterest (Pinterest's own how-to pin format, Buffer on step-by-step pins). In this niche the before/after has a real physical story the guides already tell: a drained faucet in October versus a split pipe in January. Stacked panels also read cleanly on a phone, one idea per band.
archetypes.layout: Headline y 60-290. 2 to 4 full-width panels stacked from y 320 to 1330, 16px gutters, 24px radius, alternating paper and sage-soft fills. Each panel: small-caps label at top-left (e.g. 'October' / 'January', 'Walk' / 'Write' / 'Enter' / 'Forget'), one drawing on one side, one real line of text on the other. Product line bottom-left y 1360-1450.
archetypes.visual: frozen-pipe, outdoor-faucet, paper-clutter vs lease-card, store-shelf, item-card, or the real workspace screenshot in a phone-screen in the final panel.
archetypes.text: Panel labels and lines are taken from the pin's own description or the linked guide (step names, the date-job/interval-job lists, the invoice vs diagnosis lines).
archetypes.bestFor: freeze before/after, date vs interval, broken vs due, tap/see/add, note/print/bring, walk/write/enter/forget, renter records before/after

archetypes.name: Renter's move-in photo walk-through
archetypes.clicks: Renter move-in guidance converges on one ritual: photograph every room before unpacking, wall by wall, with dates (Tellus, Happy.co, Manaky renter guides; HUD as cited in the product's own guide). A floor plan with a numbered walking route and dated photo tiles turns that ritual into a map renters can follow and save before move-in day.
archetypes.layout: Headline y 60-290. Rental floor plan x 80-920, y 320-960 with a numbered dotted route and viewfinder corners in each room. A row of 3 photo-tiles y 990-1280, slightly overlapping, each with a 'Sep 26' date stamp. Short checklist of 3-5 lines under or beside the tiles, y 1290-1400. Product line bottom-left y 1410-1460.
archetypes.text: The day-one list and the example record from the moving-into-a-rental-what-to-document guide (including its example date 'Sep 26').
archetypes.bestFor: renter move-in, deposit protection, photograph everything
